page0.text:
It's bedtime.
I don't know what happened to Saber, but the lights have gone out in that room. The sound of activity from it has gone silent.
I've heard it gets noisy when there's three girls together, and it seems that is true even when they're quiet like Saber and Sakura are.

page1.text:
"...Wait, never mind. It was mainly Fuji-nee's laughter."
Though it was still pretty noisy.
It isn't good for my mental health to have girls the same age as me being rowdy under the same roof.

page2.text:
"...Damn it. My sleepiness went away thinking about them."
Like Saber's troubled expression,
if Sakura and Saber are getting along,
or what Fuji-nee is even thinking.

page3.text: The more that I think, the more my head starts hurting. If it's like this, it might've been better if Saber slept in the room next to mine.

page4.text:
...
It's 11 PM.
The lights are out in the house, and there's not a single sound outside.
My hand goes to the door to slide it open and tiptoe by so Fuji-nee doesn't hear anything.

page5.text:
I go out to the garden.
The moon is shining bright, while the cutting breeze is cold.
In the winter night, the world was silent, as if frozen.

page6.text:
The shed has gone still.
The place where I got cornered by Lancer yesterday,
and the place where Saber appeared.
The entrance is still open, and the darkness inside feels uninviting.

page7.text:
I go inside.
Closing the door behind me to shut out the cold air, I turn on an old stove heater.

page8.text:
"...Shoot over 200 arrows, huh?"
The teaching of archery focuses on accuracy, piercing strength, and persistence.
Accuracy is how well one can hit the target.
Piercing strength is the power to pierce the target.
And lastly, persistence is how long one can maintain the accuracy and piercing strength.

page9.text:
...I think I read it somewhere in an archery manual.
Once one aims to be a shooter, after they learn the true meaning of kyudo, they continue that forever.
So they say to shoot over 200 arrows... Or something.

page10.text:
"...Yeah. I don't know what I should do as a Master, so I should at least train my magecraft."
I sit down inside the shed and take a deep breath.

page11.text:
"Haah... Haah..."
...I control my breathing and begin my regular training.
My mind imagines the same thing that it always does.
An image of a sword that comes to mind.

page12.text:
...
I ignore that and clear my mind even more.
Once I've let magical energy flow throughout my entire body, I practice Strengthening like usual.
When I was attacked by Lancer last night, I succeeded in Strengthening for the first time in a few years.
I need to repeat it so that I don't forget the sensation, or else it would be a waste.

page13.text:
"...Trace, on."
I narrow my eyes and breathe out deeply.

page14.text:
That's all for now.
I forget all about the Holy Grail War, Saber, and Tohsaka once I immerse myself into the process.
Clear all thoughts and hesitation from my mind.

page15.text:
But, during the process...
the thought that Tohsaka, who's a mage like me, might be doing the same kind of training never leaves my head.
